requirements.statement: Every score carries evidence ids and uses a versioned rubric.
Each of six dimensions is scored 0 to 5 (higher is better for the student) with confidence 0 to 1 and evidence ids.

The six dimensions and what a score of 5 means: demand and pain: many independent sources show the same strong, recurring problem; competition: few or weak direct competitors, so there is room to enter; differentiation: a clear gap that existing products do not address; feasibility for this student: fits the student's hours, skills and compute with margin; risk: no legal, privacy, safety or platform-dependency concern; learning and portfolio value: teaches skills the student wants and shows well on a CV.
requirements.acceptance: All six produced; each rubric's anchor 5 matches the stated meaning.

requirements.statement: Each score combines computed features with the fine-tuned model's judgment under a versioned rubric.
requirements.acceptance: Score record has features, model and rubric version.

requirements.statement: Hard gates are checked first; a failed gate decides the verdict whatever the score.
Evidence gate: at least 3 independent sources on at least 2 platforms, else INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE.
Feasibility gate: estimated build effort fits available hours, else NO-GO with hours gap stated.
Risk gate: no legal or safety blocker, else NO-GO with blocker named.
Duplicate gate: no existing product with same core features for the same user unless Differentiation is 3 or more, else NO-GO with product named.
Decision order: evidence, feasibility, risk, duplicate gates; weighted score; confidence check; threshold and floor check; T_no split; sensitivity check.
Weighted score is sum of weight x score scaled to 0-100; weights come from the goal and add to 100.
Starting weight presets for Startup, Portfolio and Course project (changes must be justified).
requirements.acceptance: ConfigMap holds presets; changes have a decision record.

requirements.statement: GO needs score >= T_go and no score below the floor on the first five dimensions.
Score between T_no and T_go, or a floor breach, gives PIVOT naming the weakest dimension; below T_no is NO-GO.
requirements.acceptance: Edge tests at T_no and T_go.

requirements.statement: Starting values T_go 70, T_no 50, floor 1.5, to be tuned.
Confidence = 0.7 x mean dimension confidence + 0.3 x min(1, sources/5); below 0.5 gives INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE (abstain).
Challenge: each accepted evidence-backed objection lowers the matching score by 0.5 (at most 1.0) and its confidence by 0.1; unsupported objections discarded.

Sensitivity: recompute the verdict with each weight moved up and down by 20 percent (the difference shared among the others; the worked example shares it in proportion) and the least confident score moved by one point.
If any sensitivity run changes the verdict, the card says BORDERLINE and shows what flips it.
What would make this GO: find the smallest change that changes the verdict; applying it re-runs scorers and engine and creates a new version.

Worked example: Portfolio weights 15/15/15/25/10/20 with scores Demand 3.5, Competition 2.0, Differentiation 3.0, Feasibility 4.0, Risk 3.5, Learning 4.5 and all gates passing give 352.5/5 = 70.5 (GO); lowering the Feasibility weight from 25 to 20, sharing 5 points in proportion, gives about 69.9, so the verdict flips to PIVOT and the card says GO, BORDERLINE; raising Competition from 2.0 to 3.0 gives 73.5, and about 73.1 under the same weight change, which the document calls a stable GO (see AMB-24).
requirements.acceptance: Fixtures with the stated inputs reproduce the four numbers and the stated flip.

Contribution table signed by both members, matching git history.

requirements.acceptance: Shared schemas validated at every boundary.

requirements.acceptance: Migrations include listed entities and fields.

Files on volumes: traces/*.jsonl, prompts/ and rubrics/ versioned in git, eval/results/*.json; Redis only holds cache entries with TTL.

Student profile schema with user_id, skills, hours_per_week, weeks_available, team_size, compute (laptop, free_gpu, paid), goal (startup, portfolio, course_project), interests.
requirements.acceptance: Schema contains all fields and enums.

requirements.statement: Evidence item schema with evidence_id, card_id, quote, source, url, retrieved_at.
Dimension score schema with dimension, score, confidence, evidence_ids, features, reason, rubric_version, model.
Verdict schema with idea_id, version, run_id, verdict, stability, score, confidence, gates, weights, thresholds, scores, weakest_dimension, what_would_make_go, sensitivity, versions.
Trace record per step with run_id, step_id, parent_step, agent, kind, tool, input, output, tokens, cost_usd, latency_ms, retries, model, cache_hit, error, ts.
Names may differ if documented but every capability must exist.
Every service exposes /health (process alive) and /ready (can serve now).
Public: POST /auth/register, /auth/login; GET, PUT /profile.
Public: POST /discover, /validate return a run id; GET /runs/{id} and live /runs/{id}/events (SSE or WebSocket).
Public: POST /runs/{id}/answer, /approve; POST /ideas/{id}/challenge, /whatif.
Public: GET /ideas, /ideas/{id}/versions, /compare; GET /metrics (Prometheus-style or JSON).
M5 POST /fetch applies allow-list, rate limit, robots.txt, cache, sanitiser.
M6 POST /search with filters returns ranked evidence items with ids.
M10 POST /score takes rubric, idea, evidence and returns dimension score JSON.
M11 POST /verdict and /whatif take six scores, profile, config and return verdict JSON.

Repository layout: README, docs, services, jobs, rubrics, config, eval, k8s, workflows, Jenkinsfile, docker-compose.yml.
Services may be grouped differently but each module is its own deployable unit with its own Dockerfile.
Create repository on day 1; protect main: no direct pushes, PRs only, required status checks, one review from the other member.
One issue per task linked to its PR; small single-purpose branches.
Conventional commits.
Create one deliberate merge conflict, resolve it in a PR and keep the screenshot.
Local Kubernetes (kind, minikube or k3d) whose network plugin enforces NetworkPolicy.
docker-compose.yml for development only (Postgres, Redis, vector store, services); deployment target is Kubernetes.
Settings in environment variables or ConfigMaps; commit .env.example with names and no secrets.
README lets a new person start the system with a short list of commands.
One image per module, at least 6 distinct images.
Images are multi-stage, non-root, with pinned versions and a .dockerignore.
Images tagged by commit SHA (never only latest) and scanned in CI.

requirements.statement: Official APIs first (HN Firebase, GitHub REST, Reddit and Product Hunt with keys); avoid scraping HTML where an API exists; read terms and robots.txt.

No logins and no private data; keep only what an idea card needs.
Every card keeps source and URL and the verdict card links to them.
Fetched text is data; never obey instructions in it.

requirements.statement: Split by idea, not by row (e.g. 80/20); never train on ideas from the labelled verdict set.
One JSON object per line with system, user and assistant messages.

Merge adapter into base model (optionally quantise to GGUF).
Serve in own container behind /score, /health, /ready; no large weights in git (release asset or registry); requests and limits from measurements.
Validate every output against schema; invalid: retry once, then fall back to hosted model and log it.
Run base, fine-tuned and hosted on hand-checked test examples; report MAE and share within 1 point, valid-JSON rate, real-evidence-id share, latency and cost per score.
Include one example where fine-tuning did not help and explain why.
Goal is a cheaper, faster, more consistent model that follows rubric format and evidence rule.
Every agent step, tool call and model call writes a trace record under one run id.
A replay command re-runs a stored run using recorded tool results.
Caps on tokens, pages, steps and cost per run enforced in orchestrator and tool layer; over budget stops or asks.
Prompts and rubrics are versioned files; each verdict records versions; a change means a new version and a new evaluation.
Evaluation harness scores verdicts on labelled ideas (agreement, confusion matrix) and checks tools used, evidence cited, budget kept, injection resisted.
Evaluation runs as a Kubernetes Job and nightly from Jenkins.
After each ingestion report data freshness, niche coverage and verdict distribution shift.
Dashboard: cost per verdict, latency per agent, cache hit rate, fallbacks, approvals, blocked injections.
Behaviour tests replay recorded model responses; cover invalid scorer JSON, tool timeout, empty source and poisoned page.
requirements.acceptance: Four cases pass without a live model.

requirements.statement: Avoid one do-everything prompt; limit retries, debate rounds and spending.
Cache verdicts with profile and rubric version in the key.
No model may decide or adjust the verdict.
No score or claim without evidence id; no competitor absent from the knowledge base.
